page: Amazon Web Services m7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by fourth-generation Intel Xeon 8488C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance offers direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, delivering 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs at a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz. The processor package features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and comprehensive instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for INT8 and BF16 acceleration, and AES-NI cryptographic acceleration. It does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

The memory subsystem consists of 768 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. In synthetic benchmarks, uncached large-block read operations reach 460.29 GB/sec and write operations attain 189.59 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top tier. Network capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Notably, the instance does not feature bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for operational persistence.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier multi-threaded processing and enterprise computing capacity. Multi-core evaluations record top-decile outcomes, including a stress-ng score of 171,169.26, a PassMark CPU score of 126,821.12, and Clang compilation metrics of 59,642.0. High throughput extends to memory-bound application loads, where Redis SET operations reach 192.93 million operations per second and static web serving measures 131.54 GB/sec. Furthermore, onboard AMX execution enables top-tier inference speeds on medium (7B) and large (70B) language models without dedicated GPUs.

The dense core footprint and high memory bandwidth provide substantial resource density, eliminating hypervisor contention for intensive enterprise workloads. Primary tradeoffs involve the complete absence of local NVMe storage and the single-core execution profiles that sit in middle percentiles relative to specialized compute-focused silicon. The m7i.metal-48xl is best suited for large-scale enterprise deployments, high-throughput in-memory databases, clustered compilation systems, non-GPU matrix AI inference, and bare-metal hypervisor virtualization.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 8488C processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.2 GHz, 105 MB of L3 cache, and integrated Intel AMX matrix acceleration. The memory configuration provides 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM, equating to a 4.0 GB per-core distribution, alongside 50 Gbps baseline networking. The system includes no local instance storage and no dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute, high static web serving throughput, and superior Redis key-value transaction rates, complemented by high-bandwidth memory transfer exceeding 460 GB/sec uncached reads. The m7i.metal-48xl is designed for enterprise memory-bound services, distributed database architectures, large-scale software compilation, CPU-based matrix inference, and bare-metal virtualization workloads.
